verses.text: For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David, written when Saul sent men to watch David's house so they could kill him. Rescue me from my enemies, my God. Protect me from those who attack me.
Rescue me from people who do evil. Save me from murderers.
Look, they are lying in wait to kill me. Powerful people gather together against me, LORD, but not because I have done wrong or sinned.
I have done nothing wrong, yet they hurry to attack me. Get up and help me! Look at what is happening!
LORD God of Armies, God of Israel, wake up and punish all the nations. Show no mercy to wicked traitors. Selah.
They come back in the evening, howling like dogs and prowling around the city.
Look at what spews from their mouths. Their words cut like swords. They say, "Who can hear us?"
But you, LORD, laugh at them. You make fun of all the nations.
You are my strength. I watch for you, because God is my high tower.
My God will come to meet me with his faithful love. God will let me look down on my defeated enemies.
Do not kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them with your power and bring them down, Lord, our shield.
Their mouths are full of sin, and their lips speak evil words. Let them be caught in their pride, because of the curses and lies they speak.
Destroy them in your anger. Destroy them until they are gone. Then everyone to the ends of the earth will know that God rules over Jacob. Selah.
Let them come back in the evening, howling like dogs and prowling around the city.
They wander around looking for food, and growl all night if they do not get enough.
But I will sing about your strength. In the morning I will sing loudly about your faithful love. You have been my high tower, a safe place when I am in trouble.
You are my strength. I will sing praises to you. God is my high tower, the God who shows me faithful love.
